chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Mu'alla, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whom another man on a riding animal came upon, intending to trample him, so he shouted at the animal and it bolted with its rider and threw him down, and there resulted a wound or something else. He said: “There is no liability upon him. He only drove it away in defense of himself, and it is jubar.”

key_terms.الْجُبَارُ: harm deemed uncompensated, with no liability attached
key_terms.زَجَرَ: he shouted at or drove away forcefully
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal liability or financial responsibility for harm

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if he defends himself from an attacking rider and the rider is injured after his animal bolts?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that if a person wards off an immediate threat to himself by shouting at the attacking rider’s animal, and the rider is injured as a result, the defender bears no liability. The ruling is grounded in the fact that he acted only to protect himself, and the resulting harm is treated as uncompensated.
